text:
Colorado's goalie for tonight has been the strangest number on a very good team. Scott Wedgewood saved nearly 24 goals more than expected last season; this year, in five games, he's at .867 and 5.4 goals below. He gets the start in Ottawa over Mackenzie Blackwood, who has 15 of the 19, per the Denver Post's Corey Masisak. Masisak also noticed Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar were absent from the morning skate, with nobody taking their spots in line rushes, so probably nothing. Worth checking before puck drop anyway.

Ottawa's net story runs the other way. Daily Faceoff reports Linus Ullmark returns after missing nine games, and he left at .945 with eight goals saved above expected. The Senators have also out-chanced the opponent in all five of their last five games (59% of the expected goals) and gone 3-1-1, the last a 3-2 overtime loss to Washington. They do it shorthanded: William Eklund is on injured reserve until January, Tim Stützle has slid onto the line with Dylan Cozens and Fabian Zetterlund, and Nick Cousins, Andre Burakovsky and Warren Foegele are out too.

Here's what we'd keep in mind about Colorado. The Avalanche are a real team, 53% of the expected goals at five on five and 4.11 goals a game, but they're also the lucky one tonight: their finishing is 12.7 goals better than their chances usually produce. MacKinnon is our top scorer on the board at 38%, and Devon Toews has quietly been the story of the blue line (18 points in 19 games, per the Denver Gazette's Evan Rawal). Josh Manson remains out.

Both teams have 24 points. The special teams are close (Colorado's power play makes 0.78 expected goals a game against an Ottawa kill that allows 0.80), and the Senators take 4.7 penalties a night. Small milestones on the side: Artem Zub plays his 400th game, Parker Kelly is one goal from 50 and Philip Tomasino one point from 100.
headline: Two goalies coming from opposite directions
